text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
ALITHIA
- Turkey threatens a strike against Cyprus to destroy the S-300 missiles.
- The United States seeks to defuse tension in Cyprus with its initiative.
- Real estate agent is jailed for five years for sexually harassing a minor.
CYPRUS MAIL
- Turkey beats war drums over Cyprus's missile purchase.
- U.S. initiative is 'unaffected' by the purchase of missiles, says the government.
- Unions warn they will go on strike unless cost of living allowances are paid at the end of January.
HARAVGHI
- The United States steps up pressure on Cyprus to cancel the missile deal.
- Cost of living allowances will be paid to civil servants.
- Active involvement is expected from Russia on the Cyprus issue.
PHILELEPHTHEROS
- U.S. envoy Carey Cavanaugh arrives to defuse tension in Cyprus.
- Turkey threatens Cyprus with a new 1974.
- Cyprus's grain commission seeks increases in the price of bread and flour.
SIMERINI
- Hypocrisy of the United States. It sold 22 Harpoon missiles to Turkey with two launchers last year.
- A young Egyptian waiter died after remaining for 12 hours in a ditch he fell into after a crash with his motorcycle.
